experiment: FirstTrial v4 — physics reach and HMM smoothing
scope: Exploratory scores on the same public five-minute example used in v1-v3; 7,500 graded frames and 17 ground-truth possession spells.
design: Seven fixed comparisons: prior references, an acceleration-aware player-reach prior, a fixed-prior categorical HMM, and combinations. No automatic winner selection.
interpretation: V2 shape plus movement remains the best measured Spell F1. Current pitch-control and HMM settings substantially fragmented possession spells. These results do not justify adding either to the main prediction approach.
limitations: The public sample has 17 possession spells and was used in all previous experiments; it is not independent validation.
HMM transitions and emissions are hand-set, not trained or calibrated.
The player-reach model is Spearman-inspired but omits ball-flight drag, passing choices, offside, individual player attributes, and full team-control integration.
Pitch control requires a target coordinate; safe interpolation covered only 41 missing-ball frames, so most long gaps remain unsupported.
Track slots are anonymous fragments; no named-player roles or stable identities are inferred.
Full-match performance and the best feature combination remain unknown.
